panels.title: Proxy req/s (total)
panels.description: All requests received by eBeacon — cache hits, upstream forwards, and multiplexed responses included. Use this for client-visible throughput.

panels.title: Upstream req/s
panels.description: Requests actually forwarded to a beacon node upstream. Excludes cache hits and singleflight-deduplicated requests. Compare with Proxy req/s to understand cache effectiveness.

panels.title: Cache served/s
panels.description: Responses returned directly from eBeacon's local cache without touching any upstream. High values here mean most client-visible latency is sub-millisecond.

panels.title: Error rate (5xx)
panels.description: Server-side failures: upstream responses with status_class=5xx. Client errors (4xx) are not counted here.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Hits / (hits + misses) over the rate window.

panels.title: Active upstream connections
panels.description: In-flight HTTP requests to upstreams right now (gauge). Singleflight collapses identical concurrent GETs, so this stays low even under load. Spikes between Prometheus scrapes may not appear — use the throughput graph for rate trends.

panels.title: Request / Upstream / Response rate
panels.description: Proxy req/s = all requests arriving at eBeacon. Upstream req/s = forwarded to beacon node (cache miss + not multiplexed). Cache served/s = answered from local LRU cache without upstream call. Multiplexed/s = deduplicated concurrent GETs collapsed by singleflight. The gap between Proxy and Upstream is the share served locally.

panels.title: Request duration (p50 / p90 / p99)
panels.description: End-to-end proxy duration including upstream round-trip. Cache hits are excluded (they don't go to upstream and do not appear in this histogram).

panels.title: Per-upstream health, score & traffic
panels.description: Health: 0=down, 1=degraded, 2=up. Circuit breaker: 0=closed (normal), 1=open (tripped), 2=half-open (probing). Score is the live composite routing score that combines error rate, p90 latency, head lag, and sync distance.

panels.title: Upstream health timeline
panels.description: 0=down, 1=degraded, 2=up per backend over time.

panels.title: Head slot per upstream
panels.description: Current head slot reported by each upstream. A lagging line indicates an upstream falling behind the chain tip. Divergence between upstreams can cause inconsistent responses when not using sticky routing.

panels.title: Head → finalized slot distance per upstream
panels.description: Slots between this upstream's current head and its latest finalized checkpoint (finalized_epoch * 32). Healthy value is 32–64 slots (1–2 epochs). Spikes indicate finality is stalling. All upstreams tracking the same value confirms consensus agreement.

panels.title: Upstream head slot divergence
panels.description: max(head_slot) − min(head_slot) across all upstreams. Zero means all upstreams agree on the chain tip. Non-zero values mean some upstreams are ahead of others; during normal propagation this can be 1–2 slots.

panels.title: Finalized epoch per upstream
panels.description: Latest finalized epoch per upstream. All upstreams should converge on the same value within a few seconds of each other. A stalled line here indicates a finality issue on that specific node.

panels.title: Backend sync distance
panels.description: Slots behind the network head. 0 = fully synced. Any value >0 means the node is still catching up.

panels.title: Cache size
panels.description: Number of distinct cached URLs (LRU entry count, not bytes). Only 2xx responses are stored.

panels.title: Cache hit vs non-hit by method (req/s)
panels.description: non-hit includes cache misses and bypasses (method/policy).

panels.title: Requests by API Key
panels.description: Request rate broken down by API key and network

panels.title: Requests by API Key & Status
panels.description: Request rate by API key and HTTP status class

panels.title: API Key Request Summary
panels.description: Total requests per API key over selected time range

targets.expr: sum by (api_key, network, method, status_class) (increase(ebeacon_requests_by_api_key_total{network=~"$network", api_key=~"$api_key", method=~"$method"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Latency by method (p50 / p90 / p99)
panels.description: Histogram quantiles from end-to-end proxy latency grouped by HTTP method.

panels.title: Latency by API path (p90)
panels.description: Histogram p90 latency grouped by normalized Beacon API path.

panels.title: Request volume by API path & status
Cache outcome by API path
panels.description: hit_% is relative to all cache-eligible observations for the selected normalized path set.

panels.title: Archive Routing
panels.description: Routing of historical-data requests to archive-capable upstreams.

panels.title: Archive promotions/s by reason
panels.description: Rate of requests routed to archive upstreams, broken down by why: `proactive` = target slot/epoch was demonstrably older than the per-endpoint retention window (classified before any upstream was tried); `pruning_error` = a pruned upstream returned a 404 on a historical-id path and the retry budget was promoted to archive candidates.

panels.title: Pruning 404s returned (no archive configured)
panels.description: Rate of pruning-shaped 404s returned to clients because no upstream in this network is marked archive: true. A sustained non-zero rate means clients are asking for historical data your pruned nodes cannot serve — configuring an archive upstream would convert these into successful responses.

panels.title: Archive-capable upstreams
panels.description: Per-upstream `archive` flag. A value of 1 means the upstream is eligible to serve historical-data requests promoted via archive routing; 0 means it is treated as pruned and skipped for known-historical requests.

panels.title: Archive promotions/s by network
panels.description: Per-network breakdown of archive promotion rate (sum of both reasons). Useful for finding which networks are exercising historical-data paths.

panels.title: Archive promotions vs pruning-404 no-archive events
panels.description: Overlay of archive promotions (handled) against pruning 404s returned unhandled because no archive is configured. If the orange line is persistently non-zero, the network would benefit from adding an archive: true upstream.
